title: The Ladder
intro: Forty years in this park and I have watched Pip try this every week of them, and it has never once worked. So let us do it properly.
A ladder is a chase. You put a stone on one liberty, it runs, you put it on one liberty again. It cannot ever get away, so long as nothing is waiting for it.

steps.instruction: It starts here. That white stone has two liberties. Put it on one.
steps.hint: The end of the board is that way. Count how far.
steps.explanation: Atari. It cannot stay -- so it will run, and you already know which way, because there is only one way left.

steps.instruction: It ran. Do the same thing again.
steps.hint: Same move as last time, one step along.
steps.explanation: Atari again. Notice that you have not had to think: the shape is doing the work, and every white stone added is another one you will take.

steps.instruction: And again. This is the whole of a ladder.
steps.explanation: Three stones now instead of one, and still on one liberty. A ladder does not get better for White by continuing, which is why continuing is a mistake and why they usually do.

steps.instruction: Once more. Look where the edge is before you play.
steps.hint: Keep going. The edge is close.
steps.explanation: Four stones. The board runs out before White does, and when it does they all come off together. That is the payoff, and it is the reason you must read a ladder to the end BEFORE you start one -- if a white stone were waiting down there, every one of these moves would have been a gift.

outro: That is a ladder. It works because the running stone never gains anything, and it ends because the board does.

And here is the bit Pip has never learned: read it to the end first. One white stone anywhere along that staircase and the whole thing turns round and it is you who has given away eight stones. It takes ten seconds. Take the ten seconds.
